reasonToGo: Wood grows on the seaward side of a drowned valley here and there is no way to take a log out of it but on foot, so anyone who needs a plank, a shaft or a mast walks in and out again inside one tide.

hazards.name: The drowned crossing
hazards.description: The valley the wood stands over is sea to its head and fills faster than a man carrying a log walks. The drownings here are all on the way out, never on the way in.

hazards.name: No side off the cut
hazards.description: The inland route runs the whole length of a steep-walled cut with nothing off it — no bench, no shelf, no bank a body can get up onto — so a party that meets water coming down has only the way it came.
hazards.note: Absence hazard: the harm is the way out that is not there. Nothing in the runtime enum expresses a route with no exit.

resources.name: Valley timber
resources.description: Cut on the seaward side of the drowned valley and rafted across at slack water, because the way round the head of it is three days with a log on your shoulder.

resources.name: Headland greens
resources.description: Meadow growth taken off the open headland from thaw to frost, and the reason a cutting party feeds itself off the ground instead of out of the villages' stores.

landmarks.name: Haulsound Stack
landmarks.description: A rib of rock left standing offshore on its own legs. Kept square off the bow it brings a raft in on the right side of the flats; let it drift and the flats have the raft.

landmarks.name: Ford past Cairnbreak
landmarks.description: The one crossing on the river above the wood, hard-bottomed and shallow in the season the timber comes down — which is the only season anyone is here to walk it.
